title: Slow Cooker Japanese Beef Curry
description: Rich, tender beef curry that cooks all day. Great on its own over rice or with a crispy katsu on top.

items.name: fresh ginger
items.prep: finely grated, no need to peel

items.name: Japanese curry roux
items.prep: about 1.5 boxes of 92 g Golden Curry

method.title: Brown the beef
method.instruction: Pat the beef dry. Heat half the oil in a large pan over high heat and brown the beef in batches. Transfer to the slow cooker.

method.title: Caramelise the onions
method.instruction: Lower to medium heat, add the remaining oil and the onions. Cook until deep golden and jammy. Add the garlic and ginger for the last minute.

method.title: Deglaze
method.instruction: Add a splash of the stock to the pan and scrape up the browned bits. Tip everything into the slow cooker.

method.title: Load the slow cooker
method.instruction: Push the beef to the bottom, then add the carrots, potatoes, apple, remaining stock, soy, Worcestershire and honey. The liquid won't cover everything; it rises as it cooks.

method.title: Slow cook
method.instruction: Lid on, no stirring. Cook on low for 8 hr, or 4 hr low + 2 hr high. Ready when a chunk of beef falls apart easily.

method.title: Add the roux
method.instruction: Break the roux into pieces and dissolve in a ladle of the hot cooking liquid until smooth. Stir it back in.

method.title: Thicken
method.instruction: Cook on high with the lid ajar, stirring every 5-10 min, until thickened. Taste and adjust. Switch to keep warm until serving.

details.Rinse: Swirl and drain 2-3 times until the water is only slightly cloudy.
details.Ratio: 1 cup rice to 1.25 cups water (standard cups), or fill to the bowl line for the number of rice cups (Tiger cup = 180 ml).
details.Setting: Quick (~25-30 min). Regular/sushi setting gives a better texture but takes longer.

notes: Avoid 'diced lean' beef (topside/round); it goes dry and stringy. If it's all you have, keep it on low and check at 6 hr.
One 92 g box of roux thickens ~720 ml of liquid. Start with less and add more cubes if needed; too much makes it thick and salty. It thickens further as it sits.
1 hr on high is roughly 2 hr on low. Low gives more tender beef.
Soy swaps: oyster sauce 1:1, teriyaki (drop the honey), or 1 tsp fish sauce.
Never cook the katsu in the slow cooker. Fry or air fry it while the roux thickens and serve the curry beside it so the crumb stays crisp.
Even better the next day. Loosen leftovers with a splash of water when reheating.
